records.claim: Acts 9:7 reports companions hearing a voice/sound while seeing no one. Acts 22:9 says companions saw the light and is responsibly rendered in current translations both as not hearing and as not understanding the speaker's voice. Acts 26:14 says all fell and Paul heard a voice, but does not separately state whether the companions heard it. The game therefore preserves the witness boundary rather than forcing one harmonizing theory.
All three identify Jesus as the one being persecuted; Acts 22:8 adds Jesus of Nazareth/Nazarene wording.

Acts 9:6 — enter the city and be told what to do. Acts 22:10 — go into Damascus and be told what has been assigned. Acts 26:16–18 — the retelling gives the extended servant/witness commission directly in the road dialogue.

Acts 9:8–9 — Saul cannot see, is led by hand, and remains without sight for three days. Acts 22:11 — Paul says he could not see because of the brilliance and was led by companions into Damascus. Acts 26:12–18 — this assigned unit does not state blindness or hand-leading.
Acts 9 narrator introduces Ananias' vision, visit and restoration interaction. Acts 22 Paul retells Ananias' visit and words. Acts 26:12–18 does not mention Ananias in this assigned unit.

Acts 9 — the Lord tells Ananias that Saul is a chosen instrument and Ananias later goes to him. Acts 22 — Ananias tells Paul about knowing God's will and being a witness. Acts 26 — Paul retells Jesus directly commissioning him as servant/witness in the road dialogue.

Matrix must preserve each witness separately, including Acts 26 'all fell', Acts 22:9 translation boundary, Acts 26 companion-hearing not-stated boundary, different immediate instructions, and Ananias/commission placement.

Any fully cited synthesis meeting the required dimensions, preserving Acts 9 narrator versus Paul's Acts 22/26 speeches, translation-neutral Acts 22:9 handling, Acts 26 companion-hearing boundary, and Ananias/commission provenance.
